decomposition_notes: Single-goal shape. All work is in the UI layer (token migration, toggle component, preference persistence, FOUC prevention). Tasks are ordered by code-coupling: tokens must land before the toggle component can reference them, and persistence must land before the FOUC script can read it. No cross-goal coordination required.

goals.title: Add a dark mode toggle to the app header
goals.why: Users running the app at night report eye strain; designers cannot share dark-mode mockups confidently because the current UI has no token system.
goals.what: Migrate hardcoded colors to daisyUI semantic tokens, add a header toggle that flips the data-theme attribute, persist the user's preference, and prevent first-paint flicker.
goals.description: v1 dark mode is a single binary toggle in the header that flips the entire interface to a low-light palette without a page reload, persisting the choice across sessions.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Toggle in the header flips the entire app to dark mode
Preference persists across sessions
No flash of unstyled content (FOUC) on first paint
All 14 known routes render correctly in dark mode
pitfalls: Do not introduce a new theming JS library
Do not break the existing data-theme attribute pattern

tasks.title: Migrate hardcoded colors in core_components to daisyUI semantic tokens
tasks.description: Replace bg-white, text-gray-900, border-gray-200, etc. with bg-base-100, text-base-content, border-base-300 in lib/app_web/components/core_components.ex so dark mode can swap palettes by flipping data-theme alone.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
All hardcoded Tailwind colors in core_components.ex replaced with daisyUI semantic tokens
Light-mode rendering unchanged on the 14 known routes
Grep for hardcoded Tailwind color classes returns zero hits in core_components
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use daisyUI semantic tokens listed in app.css (bg-base-100, text-base-content, border-base-300, etc.)
Do not introduce hex colors or arbitrary Tailwind values
pitfalls: Do not change component prop names or behavior — color migration only

unit_tests: Existing core_components render tests still pass unchanged after the token swap (no markup/attribute drift beyond class values)
Snapshot/render assertions for buttons, inputs, and flash confirm daisyUI token classes (bg-base-100, text-base-content, border-base-300) are emitted instead of bg-white/text-gray-900/border-gray-200
manual_tests: Walk all 14 known routes in light mode and confirm rendering is visually identical to the pre-migration baseline
edge_cases: grep -E 'bg-white|text-gray-[0-9]|border-gray-[0-9]' over core_components.ex returns zero hits (the task's verification command)
Arbitrary Tailwind values and hex colors (e.g. bg-[#fff]) are not introduced as a shortcut during the swap
testing_strategy.coverage_target: No coverage regression in core_components render tests; grep-for-hardcoded-shades returns zero matches

security_considerations: Pure CSS-class migration in core_components.ex — no auth, user input, or data-access surface is touched

tasks.title: Migrate hardcoded colors in delayed_modal to daisyUI semantic tokens
tasks.description: Same migration as the previous task, applied to lib/app_web/components/delayed_modal.ex. Necessary so modal overlays match the rest of the UI when the theme flips.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
All hardcoded Tailwind colors in delayed_modal.ex replaced with daisyUI tokens
Modal overlay backdrop uses bg-base-200/90 not bg-black/50
Light-mode modal rendering visually unchanged
tasks.patterns_to_follow: Mirror the token choices used in core_components.ex
pitfalls: Do not touch modal interaction logic — color migration only

verification_steps.step_text: Open a modal in light mode and confirm visual rendering unchanged from baseline

unit_tests: delayed_modal render tests still pass and assert the backdrop class is bg-base-200/90 rather than bg-black/50
manual_tests: Open a modal in light mode and confirm the overlay and panel render visually unchanged from the baseline screenshot (the task's verification step)
edge_cases: grep for bg-white/text-gray-*/border-gray-*/bg-black over delayed_modal.ex returns zero hits
Token choices mirror those already landed in core_components.ex (no divergent palette for the modal)
testing_strategy.coverage_target: No coverage regression in delayed_modal render tests

security_considerations: Pure CSS-class migration in delayed_modal.ex — modal interaction logic is untouched and no auth, user input, or data-access surface is involved

tasks.title: Add user_preferences.theme column for dark mode persistence
tasks.description: Add a string column theme to user_preferences (or create the table if absent) with values 'light' or 'dark'. Default 'light'. Adds the storage that the LiveView toggle will write to and the FOUC script will read from.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Migration creates or extends user_preferences with a theme string column
Default value is 'light'
User schema exposes the new field via the existing changeset
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mirror the existing migration style under priv/repo/migrations/
Use a string column with a check constraint, not an enum (daisyUI grows palettes; check constraint can widen)
pitfalls: Do not migrate existing rows — let them fall back to the default

unit_tests: User changeset casts and accepts theme values 'light' and 'dark'
Changeset (or DB check constraint) rejects an out-of-range theme value such as 'neon'
A user_preferences row created without an explicit theme defaults to 'light'
integration_tests: mix ecto.migrate runs the new migration successfully (the task's verification command)
mix ecto.rollback reverts the theme column cleanly, then re-migrates
edge_cases: Pre-existing user_preferences rows are NOT rewritten by the migration and fall back to the 'light' default
NULL theme reads back as the 'light' default rather than crashing preference lookups
testing_strategy.coverage_target: 100% of the User changeset branches touching :theme covered

security_considerations: Theme reads and writes must be scoped to the current user — a user may only read or update their own user_preferences.theme, never another user's row

Constrain theme to the 'light'/'dark' allow-list via a DB check constraint and changeset validation so an attacker cannot persist arbitrary strings into the column that later feed the FOUC script or data-theme attribute

tasks.title: Add theme_toggle LiveView component and wire it into the header
tasks.description: Add a small LiveView component that renders a sun/moon icon button. Clicking it sends a phx-click event that updates the user's preference and pushes the data-theme attribute change to the DOM via a JS hook.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Component renders in the app header
Click toggles between light/dark in under 50ms
User preference column updates atomically with the visual change
Keyboard accessible (Enter/Space activate)
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use the existing core_components button + icon idioms
Update the preference through MyApp.Accounts, not Repo directly
pitfalls: Do not flash the wrong-theme paint on toggle — push the attribute change before the LiveView re-renders

verification_steps.step_text: Click the toggle in both modes; observe no FOUC and the preference persists across reloads

unit_tests: Component renders a sun/moon icon button in the header using the existing core_components button + icon idioms
Button is keyboard operable — Enter and Space activate the toggle (accessible name / aria present)
integration_tests: phx-click toggles the theme and persists it through MyApp.Accounts (not Repo directly), and the new value survives a page reload
The data-theme attribute is pushed to the DOM via the JS hook before the LiveView re-render so no wrong-theme paint flashes on toggle
edge_cases: Rapid double-click / repeated toggles converge to a single consistent persisted value (no race between the DOM push and the Accounts write)
Toggle is exercised in both starting states (light->dark and dark->light)
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Full branch coverage of the component's handle_event toggle logic

security_considerations: The phx-click handler must derive the target user from current_scope/session, never from a client-supplied user_id, so one user cannot flip another user's theme preference
Persist the preference through MyApp.Accounts with changeset validation rather than writing to Repo directly, keeping the 'light'/'dark' allow-list enforced on the write path

tasks.title: Add FOUC-prevention script to read the theme preference before CSS loads
tasks.description: Add a tiny inline script at the top of the head that reads the theme preference (from cookie for guests, from data attribute on body for logged-in users injected server-side) and sets data-theme on the html element before stylesheets load. Eliminates the wrong-theme flash on first paint.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Inline script runs before <link rel="stylesheet"> tags
No visible wrong-theme flash on first paint in dark mode
Script is <500 bytes inline so it doesn't bloat the document head
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Server-side renders the user's preference into a data attribute on body when authenticated
Falls back to a cookie for guests so toggle works pre-login too
pitfalls: Do not load external JS for this — it MUST be inline to beat the FOUC window

verification_steps.step_text: Hard-reload in dark mode and watch for a flash — there must be none

manual_tests: Hard-reload in dark mode and watch for a wrong-theme flash — there must be none (the task's verification step)
Confirm via view-source / devtools that the inline script appears before the <link rel="stylesheet"> tags in the head
integration_tests: Authenticated request renders the user's saved preference into the body data attribute and the inline script applies it to <html> before stylesheets load
Guest request reads the preference from the cookie so the pre-login toggle still takes effect on first paint
edge_cases: JavaScript disabled / no-JS: page still renders in the server-rendered default theme without erroring
localStorage or cookie unavailable (private mode, blocked storage): script falls back to the default theme instead of throwing
Missing or unrecognized preference value falls back to 'light' rather than leaving data-theme unset
Inline script stays under the 500-byte budget so it does not bloat the document head
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Both authenticated (data-attribute) and guest (cookie) preference-source branches exercised

security_considerations: The server-rendered preference injected into the inline head script and body data attribute must be a validated 'light'/'dark' enum, never raw user input, to prevent HTML/JS injection into the <head> script context
Because this is an inline <script>, verify it is compatible with the app's Content-Security-Policy (nonce/hash) so tightening CSP later does not silently disable FOUC prevention
